speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any recent changes in your environment or new products you've used?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash has persisted for 5 months and is chronic, yet you deny new exposures or medications. To narrow the differential, have you noticed any seasonal patterns, or does the itching worsen at night or while in bed? Also, do you have any personal or family history of atopic conditions like eczema, asthma, or hay fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Psoriasis (specifically Plaque Psoriasis) presenting with pruritus on the bilateral upper extremities, likely exacerbated by stress or seasonal factors, despite the patient's confusion regarding a urinary tract infection diagnosis.
